brief: Give the night a moon to see by. MEASURED at the source this pass: applyLight()'s entire night is ONE multiply, rgba(44-16*nightF, 56-12*nightF, 112, 0.8*nightF), keyed on nightF and on nothing else — and in 17,889 lines moonLit() has exactly three consumers, the disc it draws (~L8578), the river's glitter (~L14514) and moonName (~L17005). #188 put a real 29.53-day month on the CALENDAR, one moon in every seed, and no light in the town can see it. Proof in two frames at seed 42, hour 23.00 in both: shots/mgrfull-wide.png (moonLit 0.999) and shots/mgrnew-wide.png (moonLit 0.003) differ only by the ~20 px disc. Build a real moonlight: a moonLight() scalar off moonLit() x the moon's ALTITUDE (moonArc/moonDisc already give it) x (1 - cloudCover()), and put it INSIDE applyLight's own night multiply so the whole frame lifts and cools — LAWS: the night is a composite set by the LAST thing that touches it, so a warm layer painted before the multiply is slate by midnight. Then let the surfaces that actually catch it catch it: water (drawWaterMirror already exists), snowCover, wet paving (wetF), the slates, the ice. This is 150-300 lines and a swing is welcome — take it.
successLooksLike: At the same hour on two nights a fortnight apart, one is a blue-silver night you can read the roofs and the river by and the other is black but for the lamps. BOTH ends open: a new moon under cloud must be DARKER than HEAD, so the mean night luma over a whole lunation lands within a few percent of HEAD's and the RANGE is what grew. Quote both, on a pinned ref.
avoid: Do not touch windowLit, the lamps, or anybody's behaviour — this is light, not people; that is a different brief and it would confound the measurement. Do not add an R() draw: the moon is on the calendar and must stay one moon in every seed. And watch the ground cache — if moonLight() feeds lightNow, #180's relight cadence moves; measure it against the 76.03 repaints/day bar c285 is watching and put the number in the entry. Note for your control: the two shots above are 14 days apart, so they differ in SEASON as well as phase — they are a look, not a control. Hold the instant and move the build, or hold the day and move MOON_START.
